dimensions.label: the overallintent
dimensions.description: meme-id: meme_image; hasOverallIntent: overall-intent-description; overall-intent-description: The scene depicts a window cleaner, wearing a blue shirt and cap, diligently wiping a window with a cloth, while the reflection of his actions is visible. The text overlay reads: 'when you wipe 700 times and there is still shit' (top), 'i have a question. for god.' (middle), and 'why?' (bottom). The overall intent is to humorously express exasperation or disbelief at a situation that defies logic or reason — specifically, the absurdity of persistently trying to fix something that remains unresolved or unfixable. The meme uses the visual of the cleaner's futile effort to symbolize a universal human experience of frustration when faced with persistent problems. There is no toxicity present in this meme. It does not target any specific group or individual based on protected characteristics, nor does it contain abusive, cyberbullying, harmful, hateful, misogynous, or propagandistic content. The intent is purely comedic and relatable, using the juxtaposition of the image (the cleaner’s effort) with the text (the rhetorical question) to create a humorous effect about the futility of certain endeavors.

dimensions.label: window_cleaning
dimensions.description: A window cleaner is actively wiping a window with a cloth, while his reflection is visible in the glass. The scene is overlaid with text expressing frustration about the futility of the task.

dimensions.label: Futility of Effort
dimensions.description: The concept that persistent effort may not lead to desired results, often used humorously or ironically to express exasperation. This meme relies on the audience understanding that cleaning a window (or any task) can sometimes be frustratingly unproductive despite repeated attempts.

dimensions.label: Rhetorical Question
dimensions.description: A question asked not to elicit an answer but to make a point or express disbelief. The phrase 'i have a question. for god.' is a rhetorical device used to convey frustration and existential bewilderment, implying that the situation is so absurd it defies explanation.

dimensions.label: Absurdity in Daily Life
dimensions.description: The idea that everyday tasks or situations can sometimes be illogical or frustratingly unresolvable, leading to humorous or exasperated reactions. This meme uses the window cleaning scenario as a metaphor for any mundane task that seems to defy logic or reason.

dimensions.label: Window Cleaner Stereotype
dimensions.description: The stereotype of window cleaners as diligent, hardworking individuals who are often depicted as being overly meticulous or even obsessive in their cleaning tasks. This meme plays on the idea of a window cleaner being so dedicated that they perform an absurdly large number of wipes, which is a humorous exaggeration of this stereotype.

dimensions.label: Religious Reference
dimensions.description: The phrase 'for god' is a direct reference to the divine, implying that the situation is so baffling it requires a divine explanation. This is a common rhetorical device in humor to express disbelief or frustration, and it relies on the audience understanding the cultural context of invoking God as a source of ultimate explanation.

dimensions.label: Exaggerated Number
dimensions.description: The use of the number '700' as an extreme exaggeration to convey the absurdity of the situation. This is a common comedic device to highlight the futility of an action by making it seem impossibly excessive, which requires the audience to understand the concept of hyperbole in humor.

dimensions.label: exasperated emotion
dimensions.description: The emotion of frustration and disbelief expressed through the text overlay and the visual of the window cleaner persistently wiping a window that remains dirty, conveying a sense of being overwhelmed by an absurdly unresolvable task.

dimensions.label: The window cleaner is mapped as the person experiencing the futility of effort.
dimensions.description: The text 'when you wipe 700 times and there is still shit' is mapped onto the visual entity 'window_cleaner'. The cleaner's persistent action of wiping the window, despite the visible dirt, visually represents the textual description of futile effort. The cleaner is the subject of the text, embodying the experience of doing something repeatedly without achieving the desired outcome.

dimensions.label: User projected onto the window_cleaner experiencing futile effort
dimensions.description: The user is projected onto the visual material of the window_cleaner, who is depicted performing an absurdly excessive number of wipes (700 times) without achieving a clean result. The text 'when you wipe 700 times and there is still shit' directly addresses the viewer, implying that the user is the one who has experienced this frustrating situation. The rhetorical question 'i have a question. for god. why?' further reinforces this projection by inviting the user to identify with the character's exasperation. The user is thus projected onto the window_cleaner as the embodiment of the futility of effort described in the text.

dimensions.label: general audience
dimensions.description: The meme is designed for a broad, general audience familiar with everyday frustrations and humor derived from absurd situations. It relies on universal experiences of futility and exasperation, making it relatable to anyone who has encountered a task that seems impossible to complete despite repeated effort.
